records.deidentified_narrative: the 600 block of rancho grande is a two-way roadway for north and southbound traffic. the mention block intersects with the 100 block of n. carolina and make up a ""t"" shape intersection. the mentioned intersection is controlled by a stop sign before entering the 1000 block of n. carolina. unit #1 was stopped at the stop sign waiting to make a right turn (eastbound) onto the 100 block of n. carolina. the pedestrian (unit #2) was walking westbound on the 1000 block of n. carolina and stopped at the listed intersection facing westbound. unit #1 driver stated that he observed the pedestrian walk to the edge of the side walk at the intersection and stopped walking. unit one driver advised he was at a full stop attempting to clear the n. carolina traffic to make a right turn. unit #1 driver advised since he observed the pedestrian stop at the edge of the side walk and not continue walking, the driver looked left to make sure there was no traffic coming and lightly released the brake to unit one to start making the right turn. unit one driver advised that as he looked right he observed the pedestrian walk into his car and put his left hand on top of the front of unit #1. unit one driver advised he immediately placed unit one in park and exited the car to see what was going on with the pedestrian. unit one driver advised that the pedestrian appeared to be scared and the driver asked if he was okay. unit one driver advised the pedestrian stated he was okay and wanted to continue walking. unit one driver advised that that since he observed the pedestrian to be of young age he contacted 911 to request for assistance and asked the pedestrian to wait for assistance to arrive since he seemed nervous/scared. unit one driver advised that he did not see his unit hit the pedestrian. unit one driver advised that ems arrived to the scene and took the pedestrian inside the ambulance to get him checked. unit one driver advised that a few moments later he observed the door to the ambulance open and the pedestrian jumped out of the back without using the ambulance's steps. unit one driver stated that he asked ems staff what the pedestrian condition was they said to him that he was fine with no visible injuries. unit one driver advised that the pedestrian mothers arrived and she declined any further medical assistance for the pedestrian. the officer arrived to the scene and asked the pedestrian’s mother if the pedestrian was okay and she stated: “yes, he just got scared and i think his leg hurts a little”. the officer asked the pedestrian what had appended, but the pedestrian stated he did not know how to explain. the officer walked the pedestrian to the front of unit one and asked again what had happened and the pedestrian stated that he thought the car was not going to move so he walked and then the car suddenly moved forward and hit him on his left tight. the officer asked the pedestrian what part of the vehicle he had been struck with and he stated he did not know, but did advise that he placed his left hand on the car's front end when the incident occurred and did not know how to explain how he was struck. the officer checked unit one's front end, but could not locate any visible damage (dents, scratches or broken parts). the officer did not observe any injuries on the pedestrian. the officer observed the pedestrian to be walking normal and was advised by ems on scene that the pedestrians mother declined any further medical assistance.

warrants (see listed [case id] for further warrant details). unit#2 was then transported and booked at [roadway] for the listed warrants that were verified.
